chunks: Uthman ibn Abi Shayba said: Hatam ibn Isma'il narrated to us from Muhajir ibn Mismar, from Aamir ibn Sa'd, who said: I sent with my servant Nafi' to Jabir ibn Samra, asking him to inform me of something he had heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He wrote to me: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: On the eve of Friday, when al-Aslami was stoned: 'This religion will remain established until the Hour is established, or until twelve caliphs, all from Quraysh, will rule over the people.' And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. And from Abbad ibn Ya'qoob, who said: Hatam ibn Isma'il narrated to us with its chain, the like of it. And from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hakam, who said: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Thi'b, from Muhajir ibn Mismar with its chain, the like of it.
ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about the twelve caliphs from Quraysh?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through multiple chains from the Prophet (peace be upon him), predicts the continuity of Islam until the Day of Resurrection, marked by the rule of twelve caliphs from the tribe of Quraysh. It also references a specific historical event (the stoning of al-Aslami on a Friday eve) as a contextual marker for this prophecy. In Shia scholarship, this is a foundational text for the doctrine of the Twelve Imams, with al-Nu'mani citing it to demonstrate Sunni consensus on the number and lineage of the divinely appointed leaders.
